headline: Spec-First TDD is non-negotiable for AI engineering: Stop letting AI write post-hoc tests for generated code.
summary: AI-generated tests can validate their own hallucinations, leading to false positives in development pipelines. Adopting a Spec-First Test-Driven Development approach is crucial for robust AI engineering.
details: A green pipeline can be misleading if the test suite validates its own hallucinations, especially when AI generates both the code and the tests. This creates a false sense of security regarding code quality and functionality.

The article argues against letting AI write post-hoc tests for code it just generated. This practice can lead to a self-validating loop where errors are overlooked, undermining the purpose of testing.

Instead, Spec-First Test-Driven Development (TDD) is presented as a non-negotiable methodology for AI engineering. This approach ensures that tests are written based on independent specifications before the code is developed.
By separating the test creation from the code generation process, developers can maintain higher standards of reliability and prevent AI from validating its own potential errors or 'hallucinations'.

headline_marked: [[Bhasha Academy: A Multi-Agent Hinglish Voice Tutor]] built with Murf Falcon & LiveKit
headline: Bhasha Academy: A Multi-Agent Hinglish Voice Tutor built with Murf Falcon & LiveKit
summary: Bhasha Academy is an AI-powered voice tutor designed for Indian learners, offering a private, judgment-free space to practice English and basic math in Hinglish. It leverages real-time voice and multi-agent systems.
details: Bhasha Academy is an AI-powered voice tutor created for millions of students and job seekers in India. It provides a private, judgment-free space to practice English and basic math, understanding and responding in Hinglish.

The system is voice-first, aiming to feel like a patient tutor rather than a chatbot. It uses Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite for conversations and Murf Falcon TTS for natural voice generation, all powered by LiveKit for real-time communication.

A key challenge was natural Hinglish pronunciation. The solution involved changing the system prompt to write Hindi words in Devanagari script, allowing Murf Falcon to naturally switch between Hindi and English pronunciations.

The tutor offers personalization, remembering user names and learning progress for future sessions, but only with explicit user consent. Learners can also request to have their stored profile removed, ensuring user control over data.

Bhasha Academy employs a multi-agent system, where different specialists (e.g., a math tutor) can seamlessly take over a conversation. This is achieved by passing a copy of the existing ChatContext, preserving continuity.

For situations where AI isn't enough, the system can escalate to a human teacher. If a learner struggles, Bhasha Academy can ask if they want to speak with a human, creating an escalation ticket via a Discord webhook.
